title: Not-for-Profit Integrated Review
description: Combine contributions, restrictions, expenses, endowments, financial statements, and net asset reporting.
html:
Module 5 Big Picture

Not-for-profit accounting focuses heavily on contributions, donor restrictions, net asset classification, expense reporting, and the organization's financial statements.

NFP CORE MODEL ASSETS − LIABILITIES = NET ASSETS

The Two Net Asset Classes

Without Donor Restrictions No Donor-Imposed Restriction
With Donor Restrictions Donor-Imposed Restriction Exists

Restriction vs. Condition

These two concepts must remain separate.

Restriction Controls How or When Resources May Be Used
Condition Affects Whether Contribution Revenue Is Recognized Yet
RESTRICTION → RECOGNIZE, THEN CLASSIFY CONDITION → GENERALLY WAIT UNTIL BARRIER IS SUBSTANTIALLY OVERCOME

Integrated Contribution Example

Hope Foundation receives the following during the year:

Unrestricted Cash Contribution $100,000
Contribution Restricted for Education $150,000
Conditional Grant Received Before Condition Is Met $80,000

The first contribution generally increases net assets without donor restrictions.

The second generally increases net assets with donor restrictions.

The conditional $80,000 received before the barrier has been substantially overcome is generally reported as a liability.

$100,000 → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS $150,000 → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS $80,000 CONDITIONAL CASH → LIABILITY

Release From Restriction

During the year, Hope Foundation spends $90,000 on qualifying educational costs related to the donor's restriction.

RESTRICTION SATISFIED $90,000 WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS − $90,000 WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS + $90,000

This is a reclassification between net asset classes, not another contribution.

Donated Services

Hope Foundation receives donated legal services worth $20,000.

The attorney has specialized skills and Hope Foundation would otherwise have purchased the services.

Contribution Revenue = $20,000 Legal Expense = $20,000

Donated Property

A donor contributes equipment with a fair value of $45,000.

Equipment + $45,000 Contribution Revenue + $45,000

Contributed nonfinancial assets are generally measured at fair value when recognized.

Endowment Classification

Donor Creates Endowment With Donor Restrictions
Board Designates Endowment Without Donor Restrictions

Promises to Give

UNCONDITIONAL PROMISE → GENERALLY RECOGNIZE CONDITIONAL PROMISE → GENERALLY WAIT LONG-TERM PROMISE → CONSIDER PRESENT VALUE

Expense Reporting

FUNCTION = WHY? NATURE = WHAT?
Program Services Mission Activities
Management & General Supporting Services
Fundraising Supporting Services

Financial Statement Map

Statement of Financial Position Assets, Liabilities, and Net Assets
Statement of Activities Changes in Net Assets
Statement of Cash Flows Changes in Cash

Final CPA Decision Tree

CONTRIBUTION? ↓ CONDITIONAL? YES → GENERALLY WAIT NO ↓ DONOR RESTRICTION? YES → WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS NO → WITHOUT DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Module 5 Memory Sheet

  • NFPs report net assets rather than owners' equity.
  • Donor restrictions determine net asset classification.
  • Board designations do not create donor restrictions.
  • Conditions generally affect the timing of contribution recognition.
  • Restrictions generally affect the classification and use of resources.
  • Recognizable donated services may produce both contribution revenue and expense.
  • Contributed nonfinancial assets are generally measured at fair value.
  • Long-term unconditional pledges may require present-value measurement.
  • Function means why an expense was incurred; nature means what type of expense it was.
  • The statement of activities explains changes in net assets.

quiz.prompt: An NFP receives $120,000 cash under an agreement requiring it to first serve 600 qualifying participants. The donor may require repayment if the target is not achieved. By year-end, the NFP has not met the target. How should the $120,000 generally be reported?

choices.text: As contribution revenue with donor restrictions
As contribution revenue without donor restrictions
As a board-designated component of net assets

quiz.explanation: The measurable performance barrier and the donor's right of return make the contribution conditional. Because the barrier has not been substantially met, cash already received is generally reported as a liability rather than contribution revenue.

objectives: Explain not-for-profit integrated review and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
